name: Rough Childhood
paragraphs: {first} grew up in the roughest part of {hometown}, where the only after-school program was 'running from things'.
{first} was raised in a {hometown} apartment with paper-thin walls, a broken heater and four older brothers who used {him} as a heavy bag.
By age nine, {first} had been banned from two Chuck E. Cheeses in {hometown}. By twelve, from the city bus system.
A youth counselor dragged {him} into a boxing gym to 'channel the anger'. The anger was channelled. Then it was channelled at the counselor.
{He} found a fight gym above a laundromat and never left, mostly because it had heat.
{He} started fighting in parking lots for $50 and a sandwich, then realized there were people who'd pay more than $50.
Now {he} fights like the rent is due, because it usually is.
{He} still sends half of every purse home to {his} mom, and the other half to a guy named Tito who 'knows a guy'.
{He} says {he}'s not angry anymore. {He} says this while punching a wall.

name: Former College Wrestler
paragraphs: {first} was a two-time state wrestling champion in high school and the pride of the {hometown} booster club.
{first} wrestled Division I for four years, which is the closest a human can get to being a cardio robot.
{first} started wrestling at age five because {his} dad wanted a son who could 'take a man down'. {His} dad got exactly that.
After college {he} had two options: coach middle school wrestling or get punched in the face for money. {He} chose violence.
{He} transitioned to MMA after realizing nobody pays to watch a 3-0 riding-time decision.
A gym owner spotted {him} doing double-legs on bouncers outside a bar and offered {him} a contract on a napkin.
{His} striking is a work in progress. {His} takedowns are a work of art.
Fans call {his} fights boring. {His} opponents call them 'like being held underwater by a refrigerator'.
{He} still cuts weight the old way: spitting in a cup for six hours while watching cooking shows.

name: Refugee Story
paragraphs: {first} arrived from {country} with one bag, no English and a cousin's address scribbled on a receipt.
{first} fled {country} as a kid and spent two years in a camp where the only toy was a deflated soccer ball.
{first} came to the country with nothing but {his} mother and a will to survive that borders on the medically concerning.
{He} learned the language from action movies and the sport from a free community class run by a retired marine.
{He} washed dishes at night and trained in the morning, sleeping on a gym mat for 18 months.
{He} won {his} first amateur fight with a broken hand and didn't tell anyone until the after party.
Every win is for {his} family back home. Every loss is for nobody, and {he} doesn't talk about those.
{He} has the calmest walkout music in the sport and the least calm right hand.
{He} is fiercely loyal to the people who helped {him}, and frighteningly honest with everyone else.

name: Rich Kid
paragraphs: {first} grew up in a gated community with a lake that was legally a pond.
{first}'s father owns a chain of car dealerships and {his} mother owns {his} father.
{first} went to a private school where the lacrosse team had a sommelier.
{He} got into MMA to prove {he} wasn't soft. {He} hired three coaches, a chef, a psychologist and a guy whose only job is 'vibes'.
After being expelled from two universities, {he} decided being punched was the only thing {his} dad couldn't buy {him} out of.
{He} built a private gym in the family's pool house and invited fighters to beat {him} up for cash.
Other fighters hate {him}. {He} pays for dinner anyway. They still hate {him}.
{He} is genuinely tough, which is the most annoying thing about {him}.
{He} drives a different car to every weigh-in. None of them are paid off.

name: Ex-Cop
paragraphs: {first} spent eight years as a police officer in {hometown}, mostly doing paperwork and getting yelled at by men named Gary.
{first} was a beat cop in {hometown} until a viral video of {him} taking down a fleeing suspect got more views than the local news.
{first} joined the force because {his} dad was a cop. {He} left because {he} was better at fighting than paperwork.
{He} took up jiu-jitsu for work and fell in love with choking people legally.
{He} went pro at 29, an age when most fighters are already lying about their age.
{He} quit the force on a Tuesday and had {his} first pro fight on Saturday.
{He} still writes up {his} own fight plans in incident-report format.
{He} has a mustache that refuses to be anything but professional.
Every opponent who trash-talks {him} gets a stare that has ended careers and marriages.

name: Former Bouncer
paragraphs: {first} worked the door at the worst nightclub in {hometown} for six years. Nothing in a cage scares {him}.
{first} was a bouncer at a strip club where the bachelor parties were more dangerous than any fighter.
{first} spent a decade throwing drunk finance bros onto the sidewalk of {hometown}'s nightlife district.
A regular at the club ran an MMA gym and offered {him} a free month if {he} stopped choking his clients.
{He} figured {he} was doing this for free every Friday night anyway, so why not get paid.
{He} won {his} first fight in 14 seconds and then went back to work the same night.
{His} fighting style is 'escort you out of the building'.
{He} still checks everyone's ID at {his} own press conferences.
{He} has a soft heart and hard hands. Mostly hard hands.

name: Military Veteran
paragraphs: {first} served two tours overseas before coming home to {hometown} with a medal and no idea what to do next.
{first} enlisted at 18 to escape {hometown}. {He} came back at 24 with discipline, a tattoo {he} regrets and a short fuse.
{first} was a combatives instructor in the military, which is a polite way of saying {he} beat up soldiers for a living.
A buddy from {his} unit dragged {him} to an MMA gym. {He} sparred everyone in the room and asked when the real training started.
{He} found the structure of fight camp was the only thing that felt like home.
{He} turned pro to fund {his} buddies' therapy costs, which is either heartwarming or a tax strategy.
{He} walks out to a bagpipe cover of a rap song and nobody has ever dared to make fun of it.
{He} wakes up at 4:30am every day, including Christmas, including {his} wedding.
{He} doesn't trash talk. {He} just looks at you like you're a logistics problem.

name: Failed YouTuber
paragraphs: {first} had a moderately successful YouTube channel about 'alpha male morning routines' until the algorithm moved on.
{first} once had 400,000 subscribers for a channel where {he} reviewed gas station food. {He} still has the stomach damage.
{first} used to make prank videos in {hometown} until {he} pranked the wrong guy, who happened to be a pro fighter.
Getting knocked out on camera got {him} 9 million views, so {he} decided to get good at not getting knocked out.
{He} started training 'for content', then accidentally fell in love with the sport.
{He} vlogs every training session, every meal and at least one crying breakdown per camp.
{He} is either the future of the sport or everything wrong with it. Possibly both.
{His} entrance costs more than {his} purse.
{He} will absolutely start a podcast within 48 hours of any loss.

name: The Accountant
paragraphs: {first} was a CPA in {hometown} with a 401(k), a Camry and a deep, unspoken desire to hit people.
{first} spent seven years doing taxes at a mid-sized firm. Every April 15th, a little piece of {his} soul died.
{first} was the quiet one at the office who brought homemade lunch and could deadlift the copier.
{He} started training BJJ during lunch breaks. Then dinner breaks. Then {he} stopped going back to the office.
{He} quit {his} job via a two-word email after winning an amateur tournament.
{He} entered a 'white-collar boxing' charity event, knocked out a VP of Sales and never looked back.
{He} still does {his} own taxes and those of half the roster. {He} has found some things.
{He} fights like {he} audits: methodically, patiently, until you break.
{His} nickname started as a joke. Now it's a warning.

name: Farm Kid
paragraphs: {first} grew up on a farm outside {hometown}, wrestling calves and losing to a goat named Dennis.
{first} has been lifting hay bales since age six and has the forearms of a medieval blacksmith.
{first} grew up 40 miles from the nearest gym, so {he} trained by fighting {his} brothers in the barn.
{He} drove two hours each way to the nearest MMA gym, three nights a week, in a truck held together by duct tape and prayer.
A county fair 'tough man' contest was {his} first fight. {He} won the whole thing and a ribbon.
{He} learned to fight from VHS tapes {his} uncle had of old cage fights, rewinding until the tapes snapped.
{He} says please and thank you and will absolutely break your arm.
Big city life confuses {him}. {He} once tipped a valet with a jar of homemade jam.
{His} cardio comes from a lifetime of chasing livestock that didn't want to be caught.

name: Karate Kid
paragraphs: {first} got {his} black belt at age eleven from a strip-mall karate school in {hometown} that also sold vitamins.
{first} watched too many kung-fu movies as a kid and has never fully recovered.
{first}'s parents ran a traditional dojo, so {he} learned to bow before {he} learned to walk.
Everyone laughed at {his} karate stance in {his} first pro fight. Then {he} spin-kicked a guy into next week.
{He} spent years being told traditional martial arts don't work. {He} is personally offended by this and fights accordingly.
{He} added wrestling to {his} game after getting held down for 15 minutes by a man who smelled like soup.
{His} fights are either highlight-reel knockouts or confusing 29-28 decisions.
{He} still bows to every opponent, even the ones who called {his} mom fat.
Kids at the dojo think {he}'s a superhero. {He} does nothing to correct them.

name: Bar Brawler
paragraphs: {first} has been in more bar fights than anyone in {hometown} history, and {he} claims {he}'s undefeated in them.
{first} was a regional legend in {hometown}'s bar scene. The bartenders had {his} photo on the wall like a wanted poster.
{first} got {his} first broken nose at 15, {his} second at 16 and stopped counting at 'several'.
A judge suggested {he} either take up a combat sport or take up residence in county jail. {He} chose correctly. Mostly.
Somebody told {him} you could get paid for this, which {he} called 'the best news of my life'.
{He} wandered into a gym looking for the guy who owed {him} money and left with a fight contract.
{His} technique is questionable. {His} chin is not.
{He} has never voluntarily taken a step backwards in {his} life.
Fight IQ? {He} thinks that's a type of energy drink.

name: Prison to Pro
paragraphs: {first} spent four years in state prison for a crime {he} committed as a dumb 19-year-old in {hometown}.
{first} made a lot of bad decisions in {his} early twenties, most of which ended in a courtroom.
{first} found {himself} doing time and, for the first time, actually thinking about the future.
A prison program introduced {him} to wrestling and a coach who believed in second chances.
{He} trained in a cell with a mattress and a will. {He} came out with a plan.
Inside, {he} learned discipline, grappling and how to make a burrito with a microwave and a bag of chips.
{He} talks to youth groups now, which {his} PR people love and {his} parole officer loves even more.
Every fight is a reminder of where {he} came from and where {he} refuses to go back to.
{He} doesn't trash talk. {He}'s been around people who really mean it.

name: Olympic Judoka
paragraphs: {first} represented {country} in judo at the Olympics and lost in the second round to a man who was basically a wardrobe.
{first} has been throwing people since before {he} could read. {He} still prefers it to reading.
{first} was a national judo champion in {country} with a gold medal and zero money.
{He} switched to MMA because, in {his} words, 'in judo they give you a medal, in MMA they give you a check'.
{He} realized that if you throw someone on their head in judo, you win a point. In MMA, you win the fight.
An MMA scout saw {him} launch a sparring partner through a gym wall and offered a contract on the spot.
{His} clinch is a nightmare. {His} jab is a rumor.
{He} has a very specific respect code and a very short list of people who meet it.
{He} once threw a heckler. Out of the arena. Legally.

name: Divorced Dad
paragraphs: {first} was a regular guy in {hometown} with a job, a wife and a minivan. Then {he} kept the minivan.
{first} started training at 30 after the divorce, because therapy was $200 an hour and jiu-jitsu was $99 a month.
{first} picked up MMA as a 'midlife hobby'. It became {his} whole life. {His} ex-wife is not surprised.
{He} got way better, way faster than anyone expected, possibly because of the rage.
{He} fights for child support payments and {his} kids' respect, in that order some weeks.
{He} turned pro at 32 and is somehow still improving, which annoys every 22-year-old {he} beats.
{His} kids think {he}'s the coolest person alive. {His} ex-wife's new boyfriend avoids eye contact.
{He} brings orange slices to fight camp.
Every weekend {he} has the kids, {he} also has a fight in {his} head with their stepdad.

name: Theater Kid
paragraphs: {first} was the lead in every high school musical in {hometown} and is still bitter about one specific production of Grease.
{first} studied drama in college and has a dramatic monologue ready for every possible fight outcome.
{first} spent years doing community theater before discovering the cage was the ultimate stage.
{He} realized press conferences were just improv with consequences.
{He} took a stage combat class, then a real combat class, then a third class where {he} got knocked out and loved it.
{He} trains like an actor: method, total immersion, occasionally talking in a fake accent for an entire camp.
{His} walkouts are three-act productions.
{He} cries at every win, every loss and most press conferences.
{He} is the only fighter who critiques the lighting at the venue.

name: Failed Football Player
paragraphs: {first} was a star linebacker in high school and had a scholarship until a knee injury and a bad grade in algebra ended it.
{first} played two seasons of college football and one season of 'not getting drafted'.
{first} was a semi-pro rugby player in {hometown} with more concussions than caps.
Looking for a new way to hit people, {he} discovered MMA. The hitting was the same, the helmets were gone.
{He} learned that 6 pads and a helmet are a lot of protection when you suddenly don't have them.
{He} tried out for a pro football team, got cut, and walked into an MMA gym the same afternoon.
{He} still celebrates wins with a touchdown dance.
{He} has the explosion of a linebacker and the cardio of a linebacker, which is the problem.
{He} calls every coach 'Coach' and every round 'a quarter'.

name: Fighting Family Dynasty
paragraphs: {first} comes from a family of fighters in {hometown}. Dad fought. Uncles fought. Grandma reportedly fought.
{first} is the third generation of a famous fighting family, and the pressure is enormous and mostly from {his} dad.
Every member of {first}'s family has a black belt, a cauliflower ear and a strong opinion about {his} last fight.
{He} was put on the mats before {he} could walk, and has been told how to fight by relatives at every family dinner since.
{He} turned pro at 18, the family tradition, and was expected to be champion by 25, also the family tradition.
{His} cousins fight in other promotions. Thanksgiving is a war zone.
{He} is either destined for greatness or a lifetime of disappointing {his} dad. Possibly both.
{His} corner is entirely relatives, which is great until the cutman is also {his} uncle.
{He} once had to fight {his} cousin. They don't talk about it.

name: Late Bloomer
paragraphs: {first} didn't throw a punch until age 25, when a co-worker at a {hometown} call center talked {him} into a kickboxing class.
{first} was a skinny gamer until {his} mid-twenties, when {he} decided to 'get into shape' and accidentally became dangerous.
{first} spent {his} early twenties working retail in {hometown} and not knowing what {he} wanted. Then {he} found out: violence.
{He} discovered {he} had a natural chin, which is the one thing you can't teach and the one thing you shouldn't test.
Coaches saw raw talent and an unusual willingness to get hit in the face.
{He} trained harder than anyone because {he} knew {he} had time to make up.
{His} career is a race against the clock, and the clock is undefeated.
{He} doesn't have the amateur pedigree, but {he} has something better: nothing to lose.
{He} keeps {his} old retail name tag in {his} locker as a reminder.

name: TikTok Famous
paragraphs: {first} got famous on TikTok for knocking out a heavy bag in slow motion with a sad song playing.
{first} has 2 million followers who mostly know {him} for a dance trend {he} started in a gym bathroom.
{first} went viral for a video titled 'POV: you owe me money' that was just {him} doing pad work.
Brands started sending {him} free stuff, so {he} figured {he} should probably have a real fight at some point.
{He} signed {his} first pro contract live on stream while eating a sponsored protein bar.
{He} realized that the clout lasts longer if you can actually fight, so {he} learned to actually fight. Mostly.
{His} fights trend worldwide. {His} skills trend upward, slowly.
{He} films every walkout from {his} own phone. Security has stopped trying.
{He} is the reason the promotion has a social media manager and the reason that manager drinks.
